paper_title: Self-organized clustering prediction and differential equation modeling for Alzheimer's Disease progression
core_problem: Existing predictive methods for long-term cognitive trajectory in AD fall short of accurately forecasting future scores while accounting for disease progression patterns.
methodology_summary: Development of a novel, self-organized prediction methodology that integrates differential equation modeling to forecast long-term cognitive test scores, validated against nonlinear mixed-effects models.
datasets_eval: ADNI and J-ADNI cohorts (Total sample: 1,503 in ADNI; 288 in J-ADNI).
empirical_results: Validated predictive accuracy of the proposed method for the long-term trajectory of cognitive test scores; demonstrated the simultaneous evaluation of risk factors (e.g., APOE $\epsilon$4 status, A$ eta$ status) and the evaluation of therapeutic interventions.
explicit_limitations: Most clinical studies have limitations (implied, as the text mentions 'However, most clinical...').
pipeline_steps: However, these nonlinear mixed-effects models provided during parameter estimation.
